title: Explaining landforms with interconnection and change

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches how linked processes shape a landform and how it forms over long spans or changes quickly; geo-interconnection covers general links between places and people without the landform and time-change focus, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Interconnection and change in landforms
card: This is how things link to each other. A landform is shaped by several processes working together, such as climate, rivers, rock type and people. A change in one can affect the others.
This is how a landform alters over time. Many landforms formed slowly over thousands or millions of years. Some changes can happen quickly, such as in a flood or when land is cleared.
For example, heavy rain makes a river flow faster, so it carries more soil away. If people have cleared the trees on its banks, the bank erodes even faster. Rain, river and people are all linked.
Geographers use both ideas to explain a landform. They ask what processes linked together to shape it, and how it has changed over time.
draft.remember: Interconnection asks what links to shape a landform. Change asks how it altered over time.

a.q: A gorge was cut by a river over a very long time. Which idea does this slow cutting best show?
opts: Change, as the landform formed over a long time span
Interconnection, as the river and the people are linked
Change, as landforms can only alter very slowly
Interconnection, as the river is the only process at work
a.why: The gorge formed over a long time, which is about change. The option about interconnection is tempting, but nothing in the question links several processes. Landforms can also change quickly, so slowly is not the only way.
a.clue: The question is about how long the gorge took to form.

b.q: Tom studies a creek bank near Bendigo. Farmers cleared the trees, then a storm brought heavy rain, and the bank collapsed within days. Which statement explains the collapse using both ideas?
opts: Clearing, rain and the creek linked, causing quick change
Rain alone caused quick change, so people were not involved
Clearing caused the collapse, and the rain was not linked
The bank fell because landforms only change very slowly
b.why: The clearing, the storm and the creek worked together, which is interconnection, and the bank altered within days, which is change. Blaming the rain alone ignores the link with the cleared trees.
b.clue: Look for the answer that links several causes and notes how fast it happened.

a.best: Change, as the landform formed over a long time span

b.best: Clearing, rain and the creek linked, causing quick change
